The same site icon identifies pages in browser UI; it is not part of the page body.

How the browser uses this small icon

It identifies a site in the browser: Tabs, bookmarks, and history can show the same Favicon so people can recognize a website quickly. It does not explain an action inside the page.

Verify the real browser result: After publishing, confirm that the linked asset is reachable and inspect it in tabs, bookmarks, and history; an old cache may keep the previous asset visible for a while.

It is not a Logo or UI icon

Favicon is used in browser surfaces; a Logo is a brand mark in page content; an Icon communicates a search, close, or other function. They may share a visual source, but changing one does not automatically change the others.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Replace the site's Favicon while leaving the header Logo and toolbar action icons unchanged. Check the asset referenced by rel=icon, then verify the browser tab, bookmark, and history after deployment. If the old icon remains, report the caching evidence and the next verification step.
